title: Brisk and the Missing Books
markdown:
The sun, like a warm honey drop, spilled over the jagged peaks of Ferncrown, painting the pine woods in shades of gold and emerald. Brisk the young goblin, with eyes as bright and quick as a robin’s, was out on his morning adventure. His little knapsack, always a bit grubby but never without a few smooth stones or interesting leaves, bounced against his knee. Perched on his shoulder, a small, dusky-grey shadow, was Pip, his pet bat. Pip’s tiny squeaks were a constant chatter, like pebbles rolling down a mossy bank. Brisk loved Pip more than all the shiny pebbles in the world.

“More pinecones, Pip?” Brisk whispered, his voice like rustling leaves. Pip responded with enthusiastic chirps and a flap of his leathery wings, a little dance of agreement. They were in their favourite part of the woods, where the air smelled of sweet pine sap and damp earth, and the sunlight dappled through the tall, straight pines like golden coins scattered on a green carpet. It was a place Brisk knew as well as his own cozy goblin burrow, a place that always felt safe and familiar.

As Brisk hummed a little goblin tune, a sound, faint as a whisper on the wind, drifted from further up the rocky path. It was a sort of… huffy-sputter-and-a-whirl. Brisk paused, tilting his head, his bright eyes narrowing in curiosity. He’d never heard anything quite like it. Pip stilled, his little ears twitching like tiny antennae.

“What’s that, Pip?” Brisk asked, a tiny tremble in his voice. His knees felt like wobbly jelly. This is fear, he realised, a strange, prickly feeling. He was usually happy to stick to the familiar paths, and this new sound felt… unknown. But the sound pulled him, a gentle curiosity tugging at his heart like a kite string.

The path grew steeper, the ground crunching softly under Brisk’s small boots. The air felt a little cooler, carrying the scent of wild thyme and distant moss. Suddenly, they rounded a bend and came upon a small, sun-drenched clearing. And there, amidst a scattering of colourful pebbles and a very wobbly tower of spellbooks, were two peculiar people, quite engrossed in their own world.

One was a witch, with a tall, pointed hat that seemed to defy gravity, adorned with tiny, captured dewdrop beads that sparkled like miniature rainbows. Her hands, adorned with rings that sparkled like trapped fireflies, were waving about with great enthusiasm as she spoke. She smelled delightfully of lavender and a little bit of burnt sugar, like a baking mishap that turned out rather sweet. “But it’s my recipe for fizzy-pop potions,” she exclaimed, her voice quick and high, like a bubbling stream. “It clearly says ‘three giggles and a sigh’ – you’ve put in a whole grumble! That will make them pop with a frown.”

The other was a wizard, his silvery beard so long it was practically a scarf, and it kept getting caught on his spectacles, which perched precariously on his nose. He hummed a tuneless little tune, a soft, wavering sound, and moved with a sort of slow, thoughtful grace, like a willow tree swaying in a gentle breeze. He smelled of old parchment, that comforting scent of forgotten stories, and, surprisingly, fresh rain. “A grumble adds depth, Fizzwick, dear,” he said in a voice as gentle as falling snow. “It’s for my recipe for sleepy-time spells. It needs a touch of grumble! It helps the dreams settle in, you see.”

They were arguing, but it was a rather peculiar argument, more like two playful squirrels chattering over a nut. Brisk watched, his heart thumping like a tiny drum against his ribs. Pip, sensing Brisk’s unease, nudged his ear with his tiny snout, a silent offer of comfort.

“But where’s the book?” wailed the witch, Fizzwick, her dewdrop beads rattling like tiny bells. “My ‘Fantastic Feasts and Fabulous Fancies’ is gone! I can’t find my recipe for moonbeam muffins without it! They’re simply not the same without a whisper of starlight!”

“And my ‘Whispers from the Willow and Wanderings of the Wind’ has vanished!” sighed the wizard, Glimmer, his silvery beard drooping slightly. “I’m sure the recipe for dream-dust dumplings is in there! They’re the fluffiest dumplings this side of the Whispering Woods!”

Brisk watched them, his stomach doing a little flip-flop. The witch wrung her hands, her sparkly rings catching the sunlight. The wizard tugged at his beard, looking quite perplexed. Neither of them seemed to notice the small goblin and his bat. They looked so sad, so frustrated, their faces a little cloudy. It was like seeing two very large, lost bumblebees who couldn’t find their way back to the hive.

Then, Brisk’s eyes, which were very good at spotting things, fell upon a small, leather-bound book tucked beneath a particularly fluffy patch of moss near Glimmer’s foot. It looked very much like the sort of book that might hold recipes for moonbeam muffins and dream-dust dumplings, its cover worn from many readings. And peeking out from under its cover, catching the light, was a single, familiar dewdrop bead.

As the witch started to sound like she might cry, a little sniffle escaping her lips, and the wizard looked like he was about to try and knit a rainbow to cheer her up, Brisk felt a tiny spark of courage flicker within him, like a firefly lighting up the dusk. He took a deep breath, puffing out his little goblin chest. He could hear the frantic flutter of Pip’s wings against his ear, the rough texture of his own tunic against his palm, and the sweet, earthy scent of the moss beneath his feet.

“Excuse me,” Brisk squeaked, his voice surprisingly clear, like a small bell chiming.

Fizzwick and Glimmer stopped their bickering, their heads snapping up. Their eyes widened, like startled woodland creatures.

“Oh! Goodness me!” said Glimmer, fumbling with his spectacles. “A young goblin! And a little flying friend! Well, hello there!”

“You startled me, little one!” chirped Fizzwick, her wavy hands falling still. “We were just… having a moment.”

Brisk pointed a small, green finger, his hand trembling just a little, but his voice steadier now. “That book,” he said, pointing towards the mossy hiding place, “under the moss. It looks rather like a recipe book.”

Fizzwick and Glimmer looked where he pointed. Glimmer bent down slowly, his beard a silvery river flowing over the pebbles. He gently lifted the moss, revealing the book nestled beneath. There, indeed, was a book, its leather cover embossed with constellations and swirling patterns.

“Why, bless my beard!” Glimmer exclaimed, his eyes twinkling behind his spectacles. “It’s my book! The ‘Whispers from the Willow and Wanderings of the Wind’! I was sure I’d lost it in the whirlwind of ideas!”

Fizzwick let out a gasp of delight. “And look!” she cried. She pointed to the very edge of the book, where a tiny corner of another book, bound in faded floral cloth with little embroidered flowers, was peeking out. “My ‘Fantastic Feasts and Fabulous Fancies’! They must have been tucked together all along!”

Suddenly, the tension in the air dissolved like morning mist under a bright sun. Fizzwick and Glimmer looked at each other, then at the two books, then at Brisk. A slow smile spread across Glimmer’s face, crinkling the corners of his eyes. Fizzwick let out a giggle, a true, bubbly giggle, that made her dewdrop beads dance.

“Well, whoooo could have guessed?” Glimmer chuckled, a warm, rumbling sound that seemed to fill the clearing with happiness.

“It seems we were so busy grumbling and giggling, we forgot to look properly!” Fizzwick added, her dewdrop beads tinkling merrily as she clapped her hands. She peered at Brisk, her eyes kind and curious. “Thank you, young goblin. You’ve saved our culinary creations and our peaceful afternoon!”

Brisk felt a warmth spread through him, not just from the sun on his skin, but from deep inside. He hadn’t been scared. He’d been brave. He’d helped them. Pip gave a happy little squeak and snuggled closer to Brisk’s ear.

“You’re most welcome,” Brisk mumbled, a shy smile playing on his lips, a smile that felt bigger and brighter than any pinecone he had ever collected.

Fizzwick and Glimmer, now fast friends again, began to pore over their rediscovered books, their earlier argument forgotten in the joy of their reunion. The air filled with the faint scent of lavender, burnt sugar, old parchment, and fresh rain, all mixed with the happy murmurs of two wizards and a witch planning delightful feasts and dreamy spells. Brisk and Pip watched for a moment, then, with a shared glance of contentment, turned to head back down the rocky path. The woods felt even friendlier now, the sunlight even warmer, and the familiar path seemed to welcome them home. Brisk knew he’d be back to the hidden terraces, perhaps not tomorrow, but one day soon. And next time, he knew, the unknown wouldn't feel so wobbly. He was Brisk, and he was brave.
characters: Brisk the young goblin, mountain woods companions
